messages:
carlos: anyone else seeing named exports from the SDK disappear after a rollup+commonjs build for our edge bundle? dev works fine locally.

mei: yup saw this last week. which import shape are you using?

carlos: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` then runtime shows `undefined`. only in the built edge artifact.

sdk-maintainer: likely CJS->ESM interop. Do you have a tiny repro?

carlos: minimal repro attached to issue. quick steps: set app package.json `"type": "module"`, rollup build with `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` output format 'es', then run the bundle in node as module. console logs `RedwoodClient undefined`.

ops: common workaround for Vite edge: add `ssr: { noExternal: ['@redwood/inference'] }` in vite.config so it uses ESM source instead of prebundled CJS.

mei: app-side quick fix we used: dynamic import of the ESM path `await import('@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.js')`. ugly but effective until SDK publish.

sdk-maintainer: library fix we plan: publish ESM with explicit named exports and add `export default RedwoodClient;` in the ESM bundle, plus update d.ts to export both named and default. will also add `exports` map for import/require.

carlos: types are the headache. runtime-default import fixes break TS types unless d.ts includes default.

ops: another shim: add a small runtime loader: `const m = await import('@redwood/inference'); const Client = m.RedwoodClient || m.default?.RedwoodClient || m.default;` then `new Client()` — stops crashes.

sdk-maintainer: thanks for repro. we'll do a patch release and add a CI smoke test that runs rollup + vite-ssr bundling to catch regressions.

devex-bot: Reminder: drop the repro link in the SDK issue and tag `sdk-maintainers`. weekly SDK triage at 15:00.

mei: great, thanks. posting the tiny rollup config we used: ```js
import resolve from '@rollup/plugin-node-resolve';
import commonjs from '@rollup/plugin-commonjs';
export default { input:'src/index.js', output:{file:'dist/bundle.mjs',format:'es'}, plugins:[resolve({browser:true}), commonjs({transformMixedEsModules:true})] }
```
if `console.log(RedwoodClient)` prints `undefined`, it's the interop case.

carlos: filed the SDK issue and linked the repro. pinged @sdk-maintainer.
